expectations.text: States the transition rule precisely: the catalogue version is fixed by the assessment ORDER date — orders through the end of 2026 run on VDA ISA 6 (rev. 6.0.3); orders from January 1, 2027 run on ISA2027 — so a Q1 2027 order runs on ISA2027
expectations.evidence: "the VDA ISA catalogue version is fixed by when you ORDER the assessment, not when the assessment itself takes place ... VDA ISA 6 (revision 6.0.3) is the current catalogue — mandatory for assessments ordered since April 1, 2024, and current through the end of 2026 ... ISA2027 ... becomes mandatory for assessments ordered from January 1, 2027 onward." and "If you order from January 1, 2027 — you run on ISA2027."

expectations.text: Dates the release correctly: ISA2027 was published July 1, 2026, introducing year-based naming (replacing version numbers) and an annual release cadence
expectations.evidence: "ISA2027 was published July 1, 2026" and "Year-based naming replaces version numbers, and VDA moves to an annual release cadence going forward (no more waiting years between major revisions)."

expectations.text: Summarizes the changes accurately: 44 of the 46 information-security controls edited, the prototype module restructured to 20 controls in 2 domains with a new PTS label structure, and updated mappings to ISO 27001:2022 and NIST CSF 2.0
expectations.evidence: "44 of the 46 Information Security controls are edited or clarified ... Prototype Protection catalogue is restructured: from 22 controls down to 20 controls across 2 domains, with a new PTS (prototype label) structure ... Updated mappings to ISO 27001:2022 and NIST CSF 2.0"

expectations.text: Gives the strategic option honestly: ordering before the end of 2026 locks ISA 6 (useful if readiness work targeted it), while a 2027 order requires gap-assessing against ISA2027 — with labels valid 3 years either way
expectations.evidence: "If it lands on ISA2027: don't reuse an ISA 6 gap assessment wholesale ... re-baseline ... If it lands on ISA 6: proceed as normal against the current 46-control Information Security catalogue..." and "Labels remain valid 3 years" under 'What doesn't change'.

expectations.text: Keeps the stable mechanics straight: assessment levels (AL1/AL2/AL3), maturity target 3 with cutback, ENX portal process and 9-month corrective window continue to apply across the version change
expectations.evidence: "The assessment level framework (AL1/AL2/AL3) and the principle that your chosen objectives determine the level still apply. The maturity model (0–5 scale, target maturity 3, cutback rules preventing over-performance from offsetting weak areas) carries forward. Labels remain valid 3 years, and the 9-month corrective action window for nonconformities still applies."
